modules.title: Taper Lengths & Delineation Standards
modules.description: Fundamental principles of visual guidance, taper ratios, and cone spacing per NZGTTM/CoPTTM standards.

sections.heading: 1. Lateral Shift & Merge Tapers
sections.content: Merge tapers must provide adequate visual lead-in distance for approaching motorists to decelerate or shift lanes smoothly. Always ensure delineation cones are fitted with retro-reflective sleeves in clean condition.

sections.heading: 2. Buffer Zones & Work Area Separation
sections.content: The longitudinal buffer provides an essential safety clearance between the end of the taper and the active working space. Never park plant or store equipment inside designated buffer zones.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a longitudinal buffer zone?

options.text: Storage area for site vehicles and surplus cones.
Unoccupied safety space separating the taper from the active work crew.
Designated parking space for visitor vehicles.

questions.explanation: A longitudinal buffer zone must remain entirely clear of personnel, plant, and materials to provide an errant vehicle recovery zone.

questions.question: Under wet or night-time operational conditions, what requirement applies to cone delineation?

options.text: Cones must be fitted with undamaged retro-reflective sleeves.
Any standard unreflective cone is permissible.
Reflectorized cones are only required on state highways.

questions.explanation: High-visibility retro-reflective sleeves are required to ensure continuous target-value delineation in low-light and adverse weather conditions.

modules.title: Site Hazard Identification & Daily Briefings
modules.description: Standard operating protocols for daily hazard identification, dynamic risk assessments, and crew inductions.

sections.heading: 1. Dynamic Site Conditions
sections.content: Site conditions can change rapidly due to traffic flow, weather, or work scope creep. Pre-start briefings must be held prior to commencing work and updated if site layout changes occur.

questions.question: When must a site safety briefing and hazard check be updated?

options.text: Only at the end of each calendar week.
Whenever weather conditions, work scope, or layout parameters change significantly.
Only if requested by a member of the public.
Once per contract regardless of duration.

questions.explanation: Hazard controls are dynamic; any significant change in scope, layout, or environment requires a re-briefing with all on-site personnel.
